newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA COACH LOOKS TO DAVIS CUP UPSET OVER U.S..
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA COACH LOOKS TO DAVIS CUP UPSET OVER U.S..

text.p: Australia captain John Newcombe believes team spirit will give his players an advantage as they attempt to pull off an upset in next month's Davis Cup semifinal against the United States.
The Americans have drafted world number one Pete Sampras and second-ranked Michael Chang, but non-playing captian Newcombe is putting his faith in Australian team spirit.
"As far as I know, no country has ever beaten a team with the world's number one and number two player in it so we're definitely up against it," Newcombe said on Tuesday.
"But our boys have been travelling the world together for four years and the spirit within the team is superior to any other country in the world," said the former Wimbledon champion.
"On paper they should beat us but the fact that neither Pete nor Michael have competed in the Davis Cup this year is a big plus for us," he added.
The semifinal tie will be played on hardcourt in Washington, D.C. from September 19-21. The winner will play either Italy or Sweden in the final later this year.
Sampras and Chang will be joined by Jim Courier and Alex O'Brien in a squad described by U.S. captain Tom Gullikson as "one of the strongest" teams the country has ever fielded.
Five-times Wimbledon doubles champions Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde, and singles players Mark Philippoussis, Jason Stoltenberg and Pat Rafter form Australia's squad.
Rafter and Philippoussis, ranked 14th and 15th in the world respectively, are likely to fill the two singles spots.
